haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days, each with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person then moves billing_mode to both.
haiku-low.q4: The 2% automatic trigger: new-engine charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only. Shadow errors never start rollback.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. The rollout must then pass through shadow again, and its 7-day gate starts over before the new engine can take over.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store (never charged, never written to the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current for rollback.
sonnet.q3: The 7-day shadow gate must pass: 7 consecutive days, each with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared (failed/skipped comparisons reset the count). A person makes the move, through the rollout controller.
sonnet.q4: The new engine's charge failure rate going above 2% over any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only (not shadow).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. A person must set billing_mode to shadow again and pass the 7-day shadow gate again, since the gates reset.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 after entering new_only, because the usage event log keeps events only 35 days, so the old engine could no longer reprocess the events it skipped.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED how workers learn of a change (only that billing_mode is in the config service, workers keep their last-read mode if it is unreachable, and workers may see different modes during a flip). For an in-flight invoice: every charge claims the period in the ledger before calling the provider, and a period claimed by one engine cannot be charged by the other.
sonnet.q8: Evidence location is only partly stated: the rollout record holds the gate counters, day count in both, and Finance sign-off, but where it is stored is an open question (NOT STATED). Nothing is stated that technically blocks early promotion; the gates are conditions a person checks, and the rollout controller (the only writer of billing_mode) makes each forward move.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate over a 10-minute window (provider timeouts count as failures); above 2% it starts an automatic rollback (the rollout controller runs rollback).
sonnet.q10: New-engine charging is stopped first. The old engine, in the claim-and-charge step, writes the ledger and charges only periods with no owner yet that are due, each with an idempotency key. That happens after unconfirmed charges are resolved (and skipped events reprocessed if the source was new_only), before verification and the switch to old_only.
sonnet.q11: Unconfirmed new-engine charges are looked up at the payment provider by idempotency key, and the old engine charges only periods with no owner yet (claimed in the ledger via the charge ownership record). A period owned by the new engine can't be charged by the old one; verification checks every period has exactly one owner.
sonnet.q12: The state stays RollingBack and billing_mode does not become old_only until verification passes. Each step is idempotent and can be retried. Who or what triggers the retry is NOT STATED.
